subject: science
chapter_title: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical

concepts.title: Changes Around Us
concepts.definition: An ice cube melts, milk sours, iron rusts, paper burns: change is the ordinary business of the world, and watching change closely is where chemistry begins.
concepts.key_idea: The world is a theatre of changes: our job is to tell the kinds apart.
question_patterns: list five changes you saw today
how did the ice cube change on the table
which changes can be undone and which cannot
why do we study changes in substances
classify your five changes as natural or caused
what questions do we ask about any change

solution_steps.explain: Note exactly what happens in the activity.
Write down which cases show it and which do not.
State the rule your observations reveal.

concepts.title: Physical Changes
concepts.section: A substance may change in state or shape
concepts.definition: In a physical change a substance changes its state, shape or size but keeps its identity: melted ice is still water, and folded paper is still paper, so most physical changes can be reversed.
concepts.formula: physical change = new shape or state, same substance
concepts.key_idea: Nothing new appears in a physical change: the substance re-dresses, not re-makes.
concepts.textbook_ref: gecu105.txt, A substance may change in state or shape
question_patterns: what is a physical change with examples
why is melting of ice a physical change

what changes only in a physical change

solution_steps.explain: Say what the concept means in one or two lines.
Recall the activity or example in the chapter that shows it.
Use the idea on a new example from your surroundings.

concepts.title: Chemical Changes
concepts.section: A substance may change into a new substance
concepts.definition: In a chemical change a new substance forms with new properties: burning magnesium turns to white ash, milk to curd, iron to rust; usually such changes cannot be undone by simple means.
concepts.formula: chemical change = new substance + new properties
concepts.key_idea: A chemical change re-makes matter: the signs are new colour, gas, heat, light or a permanent new material.
concepts.textbook_ref: gecu105.txt, A substance may change into a new substance
question_patterns: what is a chemical change with examples
which signs tell that a chemical change has occurred
why is burning of magnesium a chemical change
compare physical and chemical changes in a table
is souring of milk reversible why not
name two chemical changes you see daily

solution_steps.explain: Write the two ideas or groups side by side.
Note the points on which they differ and one point they share.
State in one line what the comparison teaches.

concepts.title: Slow Changes and Desirable Changes
concepts.definition: Some changes race in seconds, some creep over years, weathering of rocks, ripening of fruit; and not all changes please us, so we welcome ripening and cooking while fighting rust, decay and spoilage.
concepts.key_idea: Changes differ in speed and in welcome: knowledge tells us which to harness and which to halt.
question_patterns: give examples of slow natural changes
which changes are desirable and which undesirable
why do we call rusting undesirable
how do rocks change slowly over years
how can we slow down undesirable changes
compare fast and slow changes with examples
